newsitem.title: USA: Supreme Court unlikely to lift phone rule stay - FCC.
newsitem.headline: Supreme Court unlikely to lift phone rule stay - FCC.

text.p: The nation's top communications regulator conceded Friday that it was a "long shot" that the U.S. Supreme Court would decide to reinstate his agency's rules for opening the local phone market to competition.

Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt also held out little hope that a St. Louis appeals court would rule in favor of the FCC. The court last month suspended the agency's pricing guidelines covering the entry of long-distance companies and others into the local phone market.
"I think it's a long shot that you'd get the Eighth Circuit to change its mind on this," Hundt told a news conference, referring to the appeals court.

Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas already has declined to reinstate the FCC's "interconnection" rules. The FCC and long distance companies have appealed that decision to other members of the high court. The full court is expected to take up the issue Friday.
Hundt said that in the meantime it will be up to states to oversee the pricing conditions governing long distance entry into the local phone market.
Hundt noted that the high court is unlikely to get the case on appeal for quite some time.
He said that so far he is "encouraged" by the decisions state regulators have taken on setting the conditions for opening the local market to competition.
